cohort: A total of 22,479 parturients undergoing either vaginal or cesarean deliveries at a single institution were included.
finding: Lower predelivery platelet counts were statistically significantly associated with increased quantitative blood loss (QBL) and postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), although the observed differences in blood loss were small and their clinical significance is considered debatable.
mod_finding: The association between lower platelet count and increased quantitative blood loss (QBL) was found in both vaginal (VD) and cesarean delivery (CD) patients, with generally higher median estimated differences in QBL observed in CD patients.
